title: original-radar-dataset version 1
description: Structure of an original-radar-dataset version 1 file. It covers what both producers legitimately emit and what the consumer accepts. Producers: (1) the viewer export Review.dataset() in radar-studio-chromebook/original_sessions.js; (2) the recorder camera importer convert() in iwr6843aop-activity-recorder/original_training/camera_import.py. Consumers: (1) radar_ml.py validate()/prepare() in iwr6843aop-activity-recorder/original_training, the strict training admission described in original_training/INTEGRATION_CONTRACT.md; (2) the viewer's validateDataset(), used by its Resume (Review.restore) feature. The producer is selected by source.kind: a file with source.kind is checked against the camera_import profile and any other file against the viewer profile (see $defs/viewer_profile and $defs/camera_import_profile). Viewer Resume only accepts viewer-produced exports: every label must have source 'human', all viewer-only fields must be present, no camera_import fields may appear, and the file must match the exact source capture loaded in the viewer. A camera_import file with machine-source labels is valid here and in radar_ml, but the viewer will not resume it. Units follow field-name suffixes: *_us microseconds, *_ms milliseconds, *_seconds seconds, *_m metres, *_mps metres per second, *_mm millimetres, *_mdeg millidegrees, *_deg degrees. Integers must be JSON integers written without a fraction or exponent, because radar_ml requires a Python int and rejects 1.0 (schemas/check_schema.py checks this). Some cross-field rules cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. They are stated in descriptions and enforced by the producers' validators and by radar_ml.validate(): unique segment and label ids; label/sync-marker segment_id must name a segment in this file; start_us < end_us; label end_us and sync-marker relative_us must not exceed the last frame's relative_us in that segment; frame relative_us and sequence strictly increase within a segment; a reviewed label requires source 'human', a non-null reviewer and a timezone-qualified reviewed_at. The embedded viewer dataset_sha256 is not verified by radar_ml (JS/Python number serialisation differs).

segments.description: Sensor-time segments. Each segment has its own timebase: frames[].relative_us counts from that segment's first frame. Segment ids must be unique (not expressible here). The viewer emits at most 256 segments and camera_import exactly one. radar_ml accepts 1 to 2000. minItems 1 is the consumer's rule: the viewer can export a diagnostics-only file with zero segments, and its own Resume accepts that file, but radar_ml.validate rejects it and this schema does too.

labels.description: Interval annotations. radar_ml accepts at most 20000 and the viewer emits at most 10000. Label ids must be unique, and each segment_id must name a segment in this file (not expressible here).

annotation_audit.description: Viewer only. Append-only edit log, at most 20000 entries. radar_ml ignores it.

sync_markers.description: Viewer only. Unsynchronised sensor-time notes, at most 1000. radar_ml passes them through untouched.

diagnostics.description: Producer-specific capture/import diagnostics. The shape depends on the producer profile. radar_ml passes it through as source_diagnostics.

provenance.description: Producer-specific provenance assertions. The shape depends on the producer profile. Assertions here are not authentication.

dataset_sha256.description: Viewer only, and required by Resume. Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the viewer's canonical JSON (sorted keys) of every other top-level field. radar_ml does not verify it.

absent.description: The key must be absent: this producer never emits it.

nonce32.description: Firmware pair nonce: 32 lowercase hex characters.

uint.description: Non-negative integer no larger than JavaScript Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER.

time_us.description: Microseconds of sensor time relative to the segment origin (integer, 0 to 10^12 as radar_ml allows).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time with an explicit timezone, as produced by JavaScript Date.toISOString() (e.g. 2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z). radar_ml requires a timezone. The viewer requires at most 40 characters that Date.parse accepts.

text.description: Non-blank string of at most 4096 characters (radar_ml text()).

short_text.description: Viewer text(): non-blank, at most 100 characters, no C0 control characters.

note_text.description: Viewer text(x,200): non-blank, at most 200 characters, no C0 control characters.

xyz_m.description: [x, y, z] in metres in the sensor frame (sensor_xyz_m) or the declared world frame (world_xyz_m); y is the forward axis.

source.description: Origin of the radar data. Keys are the union of both producers. The viewer adds capture_version/firmware_version/build_id and camera_import adds kind.

sha256.description: Viewer: SHA-256 of the exact original-radar-capture JSON text that was loaded. camera_import: SHA-256 of radar_ml canonical JSON over the session-start/end file hashes and every completed-file receipt (raw lanes and video). It identifies the source; it does not authenticate it.

coordinate_frame.description: Detections use sensor-frame coordinates in metres.

timing_basis.description: Times are sensor-clock microseconds relative to each segment's origin.

capture_version.description: Viewer only. Version of the original-radar-capture file that was imported.

firmware_version.description: Viewer only. Firmware version from the capture's self-test/identity report, or null.

build_id.description: Viewer only. Firmware build id from the capture's self-test/identity report, or null.

kind.description: camera_import only. Marks a verified local camera+radar recording bundle and selects the camera_import profile.

mount_input.description: Declared (not measured) sensor mounting, as confirmed by the operator.

bracket_top_mm.description: Height of the bracket top above the floor, millimetres.

antenna_offset_mm.description: Vertical antenna offset from the bracket top in millimetres, or null if unknown.

confirmed.description: The operator confirmed the declared mount.

session.description: Outer recording session. All of its segments form one indivisible train/test split group in radar_ml. Keys are the union of both producers. name, prompt, viewer_version and mount_input are viewer only.

id.description: Outer session id. This is not the firmware session_id. Viewer: the operator id or 'session-' plus the first 20 hex characters of source.sha256 (at most 100 characters). camera_import: the bundle's session-start session_id.

participant_group.description: Participant group pseudonym, or null. Null is valid export metadata but blocks a radar_ml split. camera_import always emits a string.

prompt.description: Viewer only. The activity the operator prompted. It is never label truth.

synthetic.description: Explicit declaration that the data is synthetic (true) or a real recording (false).

viewer_version.description: Viewer only. Viewer release that produced the export, e.g. 0.9.0-preview.5.

mount_input.description: Viewer only. Declared mounting copied from the capture, or null.

config_identity.description: Configuration identity, excluding random session ids. Viewer: canonical JSON text of {protocol, firmware_version, build_id, profile, mount_input}, at most 2000 characters. camera_import: SHA-256 of radar_ml canonical JSON of {firmware_version, build_id, mount, range_bin_m, velocity_bin_mps}.

segment.description: One sensor timebase. Keys are the union of both producers. connection_epoch, data_generation, config_generation and origin_timestamp_us are viewer only. Segment ids must be unique within the file (not expressible here). The consumer requires at most 100000 frames across all segments.

id.description: Segment id. Viewer: 'segment-N'. camera_import: 'camera-<video file>-<firmware session_id>'.

session_id.description: Firmware session_id of the radar run. This is not session.id. radar_ml also tolerates a string, but neither producer emits one.

connection_epoch.description: Viewer only. Host connection epoch of the admitted frames.

data_generation.description: Viewer only. Host data-port generation of the admitted frames.

origin_timestamp_us.description: Viewer only. Firmware timestamp_us of the segment's first frame, in microseconds. frames[].relative_us counts from this value.

frames.description: Frames in sensor-time order. relative_us and sequence must strictly increase (not expressible here).

frame_common.description: Fields that radar_ml.validate requires of every frame. Each producer profile defines the full frame shape. Frames that fail radar_ml's measurement gates make windows unusable; they do not make the file invalid.

relative_us.description: Sensor microseconds since the segment's first frame; the first frame has 0. Strictly increasing within a segment.

sequence.description: Firmware frame sequence number. Strictly increasing within a segment. Gaps are diagnosed, not filled.

label.description: One annotated interval. Keys are the union of both producers; camera_proposal_index is camera_import only. Rules not expressible here: id is unique; segment_id names an existing segment; start_us < end_us; end_us <= the last frames[].relative_us of that segment (camera_import also clips start_us to observed frames). review_status 'reviewed' requires source 'human', a non-null reviewer and a timezone-qualified reviewed_at. Only reviewed human labels from the task's training vocabulary (not 'unknown') supply training truth in radar_ml. The task-to-label vocabulary rule is encoded below.

id.description: Label id, unique within the file. Viewer: 'label-N'. camera_import: 'camera-<index in the review file>'.

segment_id.description: Id of the segment whose timebase start_us/end_us use.

start_us.description: Interval start, microseconds relative to the segment origin. Must be < end_us.

end_us.description: Interval end, microseconds relative to the segment origin. Must be > start_us and <= the segment's last frame relative_us.

task.description: Annotation axis. Activity states and transition events are separate tasks, not mutually exclusive classes.

label.description: Label from the task's vocabulary. activity: walking, standing, sitting, unknown. transition: stand_up, sit_down, motion_onset, none, unknown. 'unknown' never supplies training truth. radar_ml would also accept null, but neither producer emits it.

review_status.description: Human review state. 'reviewed' requires source 'human' plus reviewer and reviewed_at.

reviewer.description: Reviewer pseudonym, or null. It is required (non-null) when review_status is 'reviewed', and in viewer exports also when it is 'excluded'.

reviewed_at.description: Time of the review decision, or null. It is required (non-null, with a timezone) when review_status is 'reviewed'.

source.description: Who asserted the label. The viewer emits only 'human'. camera_import emits 'machine' for unreviewed camera proposals and 'human' for reviewed labels.

timing_uncertainty_ms.description: Boundary timing uncertainty in milliseconds (0 to 60000), or null. radar_ml then applies a 250 ms inward buffer. The viewer emits null. camera_import emits the alignment uncertainty plus the review boundary uncertainty.

camera_proposal_index.description: camera_import only. The camera review label's proposal_index: the index of the machine proposal this interval started from, or null for a manually added interval. camera_import copies it from the review file without checking it.

audit_value.description: Audit payload value: null, a number, or viewer text of at most 200 characters.

audit_entry.description: Viewer only. One edit to the review. Each entry except an undo carries details. An undo entry carries reverted_revision instead.

action.description: Edit kind. The current viewer emits 'begin', 'end', 'review:<label id>:<reviewed|excluded|unreviewed>', 'sync_marker' and 'undo' ('edit' is the unused default).

at.description: Host wall-clock time of the edit (Date.toISOString()).

reverted_revision.description: Undo entries only. The revision whose prior state was restored.

audit_details.description: Arguments of a viewer edit: begin {segment_id,start_us,task,label}; end {segment_id,start_us,task,label,end_us}; review {id,status,reviewer,previous}; sync_marker {segment_id,relative_us,note}.

previous.description: Review edits only. Snapshot of the label before the edit.

sync_marker.description: Viewer only. A note at a sensor time. It is explicitly not synchronised to any external clock. segment_id must name an existing segment, and relative_us must not exceed that segment's last frame relative_us (not expressible here).

relative_us.description: Microseconds relative to the segment origin.

synchronized.description: Always false in v1. No external clock mapping is claimed.

external_time_ms.description: Always null in v1 (would be milliseconds).

uncertainty_ms.description: Always null in v1 (would be milliseconds).

viewer_frame.description: Viewer reduced frame. It holds only the fields the viewer copies from raw-byte-corroborated admitted frames.

relative_us.description: Sensor microseconds since the segment origin.

quality.description: Firmware quality bit mask. radar_ml rejects windows with mask & 19.

truncated.description: True when the firmware detected more targets than it reported.

power.description: Native firmware power units. This is not SNR.

sensor_xyz_m.description: Exploratory sensor-frame coordinates in metres, or null when the viewer judged the spatial estimate invalid (zero phasors, invalid flags, negative forward y, or a range mismatch).

spatial_flags.description: Firmware spatial flag bits. Bits 0 and 1 (mask 3) mean a valid estimate.

viewer_segment.description: Viewer segment. One is created per (connection_epoch, data_generation, pair_nonce, config_generation, firmware session_id). The viewer emits at most 256 frames per segment and at most 256 frames in total across segments (not expressible here).

viewer_label.description: Viewer label. source is always 'human' because the viewer only records operator intervals. Rules not expressible here: when review_status is 'unreviewed', reviewer and reviewed_at must both be null; when it is 'reviewed' or 'excluded', both must be non-null.

viewer_diagnostics.description: Viewer capture diagnostics computed by loadCapture(). They are counts and messages only and never positions.

control_parse_issues.description: Control-lane parse issue messages ('<message> at line N'). At most 512 are kept.

data_parse_issues.description: Data-lane parse issue messages ('<message> at line N'). At most 512 are kept.

dropped_parse_issue_details.description: Issue messages dropped beyond the 512-per-lane limit.

unsaved_byte_count.description: Bytes the capture tool could not save (control plus data).

viewer_provenance.description: Viewer provenance statements. The viewer emits fixed text for each.

coordinates.description: Currently 'exploratory sensor coordinates; no measured phase/axis calibration'.

license_status.description: Rights statement. This is not consent metadata.

raw_and_video_included.description: Raw bytes and video are never embedded in the derived dataset.

viewer_profile.description: Profile for files from the viewer, Review.dataset() in original_sessions.js. These are the files its Resume feature (validateDataset) accepts. Every key is closed and every label is human-sourced.

camera_frame.description: camera_import frame: the raw firmware original-radar-v2 frame record copied verbatim from the verified data lane, plus relative_us. Additional properties are allowed because camera_import does not strip raw fields, and radar_ml ignores fields it does not read. The firmware fields known from json_output.c are modeled below. The ones not required here are emitted by the firmware but missing from the test fixtures.

session_id.description: Firmware session id. Equal to the segment session_id.

timestamp_us.description: Raw firmware sensor time in microseconds. relative_us = timestamp_us - the first frame's timestamp_us.

relative_us.description: Added by camera_import: sensor microseconds since the segment's first frame.

count.description: Number of reported detections. Equal to the length of detections.

detected_count.description: Number of detections the firmware found. At least count.

session_seconds.description: Bounded session length in seconds (0 means continuous).

timestamp_basis.description: Firmware clock basis of timestamp_us, e.g. 'session_elapsed'.

velocity_bin_mps.description: Velocity bin size, metres per second.

camera_detection.description: Raw firmware detection, copied verbatim. Additional raw fields pass through. power, phasors, world_xyz_m and activity are emitted by the firmware but missing from the test fixtures.

sensor_xyz_m.description: Firmware sensor-frame estimate in metres, or null.

spatial_flags.description: Firmware spatial flag bits. Mask 3 means a valid estimate.

power.description: Native firmware power units. This is not SNR.

world_xyz_m.description: World-frame estimate in metres, or null when world height is not valid.

activity.description: Always null. The firmware never classifies activity.

camera_segment.description: camera_import segment. It holds only the frames inside the human-matched alignment window of the matched radar run.

camera_label.description: camera_import label. It is always an activity interval mapped from video seconds through the affine alignment. Rules not expressible here: unreviewed labels are source 'machine'; reviewed labels are source 'human' with reviewer and reviewed_at. camera_import copies reviewer and reviewed_at from the review file even for unreviewed labels, so an unreviewed camera label may carry a reviewer, unlike the viewer.

camera_file_receipt.description: radar-camera-file completed-file receipt (<file>.meta.json), copied verbatim. camera_import checked byte_count and sha256 against the file bytes. Additional recorder fields pass through.

file.description: Bundle-relative file name with no directory part.

session_id.description: Bundle session id. Equal to session.id.

global_byte_start.description: Offset of this file's first byte in the concatenated lane, bytes.

global_byte_end.description: Offset just past this file's last byte in the concatenated lane, bytes.

started_at.description: Recorder host clock reading ({host_utc_ms, host_monotonic_ms}, milliseconds). These are absolute host times; review them before publishing.

ended_at.description: Recorder host clock reading ({host_utc_ms, host_monotonic_ms}, milliseconds).

camera_alignment.description: Camera review alignment, copied verbatim from the review file. camera_import re-fits it from the anchors and rejects any mismatch. The mapping is sensor_us = video_to_sensor_offset_us + video_to_sensor_scale * video_seconds * 1e6. Additional review fields pass through.

radar_run.description: The firmware radar run whose frames were imported.

anchors.description: Human-matched events in both clocks. They span at least 1 second and increase in both clocks (not expressible here).

video_to_sensor_scale.description: Clock scale. camera_import rejects a deviation from 1 greater than 1%.

uncertainty_us.description: Maximum fit residual plus the largest anchor uncertainty, microseconds.

valid_video_start_seconds.description: First anchor's video time, seconds. Nothing earlier is mapped.

valid_video_end_seconds.description: Last anchor's video time, seconds. Nothing later is mapped.

drift_ppm.description: Clock drift, parts per million (camera review tool).

max_residual_us.description: Maximum anchor fit residual, microseconds (camera review tool).

camera_provenance.description: camera_import provenance. Byte integrity was verified. Authenticity and physical sync accuracy were not.

review_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the camera review file bytes.

video_receipt.description: Receipt of the reviewed video file. The video bytes are not embedded.

raw_receipts.description: Receipts of every radar-control and radar-data raw lane file, in lane order. Their offsets are contiguous (not expressible here).

machine_proposals.description: Camera model proposals, copied verbatim from the review file (default []). They are never label truth.

camera.description: Camera description copied from session-start.json (for example actual_label and settings), or null. It may contain a device label; review it before publishing.

measurement_gates.description: Statement that radar_ml.prepare gates are unchanged and camera predictions are not admitted automatically.

camera_import_profile.description: Profile for files from the recorder, camera_import.py convert(). It is selected by source.kind. There is exactly one segment, all labels are activity labels, and viewer-only keys are forbidden. The viewer's Resume rejects these files.
